title: Rocket Lab to test Space Force data network connection in orbit in 2027
summary: Rocket Lab plans to test a data network connection for the U.S. Space Force in orbit using a Photon spacecraft in 2027. The test will assess interoperability with SpaceX's Space Data Network infrastructure.

title: Eoptic, Inc. Selected to Supply DeepScan™ Imaging Payloads Scheduled for Launch in 2027
summary: Eoptic, Inc. has been chosen to supply DeepScan™ imaging payloads for a launch scheduled in 2027. The company, based in Rochester, NY, specializes in advanced multi-spectral and multi-modal imaging systems.

title: New report takes closer look at the Space Force spending surge
summary: A new report by Aerospace Corp. reveals that the U.S. Space Force's spending surge is primarily driven by classified programs, target tracking, missile warning, and command and control systems. The analysis highlights a significant focus on enhancing national security and space domain awareness.

title: NRO to expand use of HawkEye 360’s satellite intelligence
summary: The National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) has expanded its contract with HawkEye 360 to increase access to satellite data for locating radars, ships, and other electronic emitters. This move enhances the U.S. government's intelligence and surveillance capabilities.

title: HEO to use Planet satellites for non-Earth imaging
summary: HEO, an Australian company specializing in non-Earth imaging of spacecraft, has partnered with Planet to utilize its satellite data. This collaboration aims to enhance HEO's capabilities in monitoring and analyzing objects in space.

title: New EU sanctions target leaders of Russia’s space industry
summary: The European Union has imposed sanctions targeting the head of a Roscosmos subsidiary involved in developing a synthetic aperture radar satellite system for Russia's military. This action is part of broader EU measures against Russia's space industry.

title: ULA names Peller as new CEO
summary: United Launch Alliance (ULA) has appointed Mark Peller, a long-time executive, as its new CEO. The announcement marks a leadership transition within the company.

title: L3Harris names space sector leader Sam Mehta CEO after Kubasik steps down
summary: L3Harris has appointed Sam Mehta as CEO of its space sector following the departure of Christopher Kubasik due to an unspecified conduct investigation. The leadership change comes after an internal board review.

title: The 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026) is the One Space Event You Cannot Miss
summary: The 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026) is highlighted as a must-attend event for the global space community, marking over 75 years of annual gatherings.

title: SEOPS adds second Waymaker rideshare mission
summary: SEOPS has announced a second Waymaker rideshare mission due to high demand, following the initial mission announced less than three months ago.

title: Forget 'Halo' — the latest 'Futurama' episode has a ring world covered in super-intelligent rats (exclusive)
summary: A new 'Futurama' episode features a ring-shaped world called 'Wheel World' inhabited by super-intelligent rats. The creative twist parodies sci-fi concepts with humor and animation.

title: NASA astronaut and 1st female French spacewalker remove failed ISS antenna but run out of time for replacement
summary: NASA astronaut Anil Menon and French astronaut Sophie Adenot removed a failed antenna during a spacewalk at the International Space Station but did not have time to install a replacement. The spacewalk took place on August 18, 2026.

title: Starship lives! SpaceX craft arrives at Christmas Island after 24-day ocean ordeal
summary: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft has been successfully recovered by recovery teams after a 24-day ocean ordeal following its test launch and splashdown. The vehicle arrived at calmer waters off the coast of Christmas Island.

title: Watch SpaceX launch its 100th mission of the year tonight
summary: SpaceX is set to launch its 100th mission of the year tonight (Aug. 18), and the event will be livestreamed.

title: Hydrogen-powered 'rocket car' tops 400 mph in record-breaking test (video)
summary: The JCB Hydromax, a hydrogen-powered vehicle, achieved over 400 mph in a record-breaking test in Utah, becoming the fastest hydrogen-powered car ever recorded. This milestone highlights advancements in hydrogen fuel technology for high-speed applications.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 18, 1868: Total solar eclipse leads to discovery of helium
summary: A total solar eclipse on August 18, 1868, led to the discovery of helium. This historical event marked the first identification of the element.

title: Hubble, James Webb Space Telescope team up to capture the 'Black Eye Galaxy' | Space photo of the day for Aug. 18, 2026
summary: The Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes collaborated to capture a composite image of the 'Black Eye Galaxy'. This collaboration highlights the combined capabilities of the two iconic space observatories.

title: It's harder to poop in space. Scientists may finally know why
summary: Scientists have identified reasons why astronauts struggle with bowel movements in space, highlighting how spaceflight affects the human body. This issue is part of broader physiological challenges faced during space missions.

title: See gorgeous views of the Aug. 12 total solar eclipse captured from space
summary: Orbiting spacecraft captured stunning images of the Aug. 12 total solar eclipse, showing the moon's shadow darkening Earth. The event provided a rare and breathtaking view from space.

title: NASA’s LRO Images Falcon 9 Crater on Moon, Learns New Details
summary: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) captured images of a new crater on the Moon formed by a SpaceX Falcon 9 upper stage impact on August 5, following its January 2025 launch of the Firefly Blue Ghost 1 mission.

title: NASA Student Aviation Challenge Focuses on Nation’s Infrastructure
summary: NASA's Gateways to Blue Skies competition challenges collegiate teams to design aircraft for inspecting national infrastructure like bridges and tunnels by 2035. The goal is to enhance safety, reliability, and cost-efficiency while supporting economic and competitive priorities.

title: NASA’s B777 Gets New Coat of Paint
summary: NASA's Boeing 777 has received a new paint job and will replace the retired DC-8 aircraft. The B777 is set to begin operations from NASA's Langley Research Center in 2027.

title: NASA Glenn’s Legacy Forged Through Decades of Flight Research
summary: NASA Glenn Research Center has driven decades of aerospace innovation through flight research, testing aircraft in targeted environments like icing clouds to gather critical in-flight data.

title: APOD: 2026 August 18 – Perseids from Perseus
summary: APOD features an image of the Perseids meteor shower from the constellation Perseus. The Moon's phase is highlighted as a key factor for the visibility of the meteor shower.

title: Lala Batters Hawaii
summary: A powerful category 1 hurricane named Lala struck Hawaii, bringing extreme rainfall and damaging winds to the state, particularly affecting the Island of Hawaiʻi.

title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 4975-4981: Happy 14th Landing Anniversary
summary: The Curiosity team celebrated the 14th anniversary of the Mars rover's landing. The milestone was marked with reflections on the mission's journey and achievements.

title: NASA Selects Companies to Provide Payload Processing Services
summary: NASA has selected four companies to provide payload processing services under the Spacecraft Processing Operations Contract on-ramp provision, enabling commercial payload processing for agency missions from multiple launch locations.

title: NASA Mission Studies Air Pollution Over Ethiopia
summary: NASA-funded research has provided detailed long-term data on black carbon pollution in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, showing variations by time of day and season. The study highlights the impact of sources like fires and diesel vehicles on air quality.

title: Next Generation of Planetary Scientists Learn Public Engagement Skills
summary: A world-class laboratory called FORCE trains the next generation of planetary scientists in public engagement skills. The lab uses high-pressure experimental equipment to simulate conditions deep within Earth and other planetary bodies for research.

title: Ship 40 arrives at Christmas Island, Plans Return to Starbase
summary: SpaceX has successfully guided Starship Ship 40 to a location off the coast of Christmas Island. The company plans to return the ship to Starbase for further operations.

title: Launch Preview: Chang’e 7 headlines week of Chinese and Starlink launches
summary: China is preparing for the Chang'e 7 mission following a recent launch failure of the Chang Zheng 7A rocket. The week also includes multiple launches by China and SpaceX's Starlink.

title: Firefly promote next block of Alpha amid Eclipse progress
summary: Firefly Aerospace is advancing development of its next-generation medium-lift rocket while also promoting its upcoming Alpha rocket block. The company is making progress on multiple fronts, including the Eclipse program.

title: Blue Origin overviews plan for dual pad ops at Cape Canaveral
summary: Blue Origin is planning dual launch pad operations at Cape Canaveral while restoring its primary pad at LC-36A. The company has outlined its strategy for expanded launch capabilities.

title: Rocket Lab advances via series of announcements
summary: Rocket Lab has established a new subsidiary in Germany and introduced a containerized mobile launch system. These announcements highlight the company's expansion and innovation in the space industry.

title: Amid failure, Wenchang celebrates milestone as China launches AI satellites and prepares for lunar south pole mission
summary: China's Wenchang Space Launch Site marked its 50th launch milestone while also experiencing a failure. The site launched AI satellites and is preparing for a lunar south pole mission.

title: Starbase Production lining up future vehicles
summary: SpaceX's Starbase production site is progressing with multiple Starship vehicles. Teams are actively working on future vehicle production.

title: Launch Preview: Chinese failure opens busy international launch salvo
summary: A Chinese launch failure marked the start of an intense week with four international launches across three countries. The event highlights the global competition and activity in the space industry.

title: Artemis progress building lunar return roadmap
summary: NASA has released updates on the Artemis program, detailing progress in building a roadmap for returning humans to the Moon. The updates include plans for commercial robotic lunar missions.

title: Blue Origin working engine resolutions and dual pad future
summary: Blue Origin is nearing the end of its investigation into a catastrophic engine explosion. The company is also planning for a dual launch pad future.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates its 50th anniversary by releasing a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements over the past five decades. The publication showcases the agency's milestones in space exploration and technology.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return. The project aims to advance reusable spaceflight capabilities in Europe.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3, a mission by the European Space Agency (ESA), will create an artificial solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona just hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. The mission aims to observe the Sun's outer atmosphere with unprecedented precision.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 will experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event highlights the satellite's precise orbital alignment and observational capabilities.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by creating artificial eclipses and digital simulations to observe the Sun's corona. This effort is crucial for advancing solar science despite the rarity and brief duration of natural eclipses.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: ESA is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This is a unique opportunity to test software in a real deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency’s technical centre in the Netherlands.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will demonstrate formation flying by having a coronagraph block the Sun to study the solar corona, simulating an eclipse. The mission aims to test precise satellite positioning for future space science and exploration.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will be held on 16–17 September at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands, bringing together startup companies and Europe's space industry to exchange ideas and explore collaborations.

title: Deep Dive: FY27 Defense Space Budget
summary: The U.S. Space Force's FY27 budget request has been highlighted as a record-breaking $71.3 billion. This budget request has drawn significant attention in the space industry.

title: Slingshot’s Portal Adds New AI-Powered Missions
summary: Slingshot Aerospace has enhanced its Portal platform with AI-powered capabilities to improve monitoring of the increasingly crowded space environment. The update aims to assist operators in managing space traffic more effectively.

title: HEO Taps Planet Labs to Expand its NEI Network
summary: HEO has partnered with Planet Labs to expand its NEI network to over 50 in-space sensors, enabling more frequent and high-resolution imaging of objects in orbit from multiple angles.

title: DIU, SDA Select Winners for Deorbit-as-a-Service Designs
summary: The Space Development Agency (SDA) and Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) selected three companies to design scalable satellite capabilities for rendezvous, capture, and deorbit. This initiative aims to enhance satellite servicing and debris mitigation in orbit.
company: Space Development Agency (SDA) and Defense Innovation Unit (DIU)

title: SEOPS Doubles Down on Waymaker Dedicated Rideshare Program
summary: SEOPS is expanding its Waymaker dedicated rideshare program as SpaceX's Transporter program ends, aiming to fill a gap for cost-effective rides to orbit for space startups.

title: The New Middle Ground in Spacecraft Development
summary: The commercial space industry is shifting focus from affordability to customers building their own spacecraft hardware for full mission ownership. This trend represents a new middle ground in spacecraft development.

title: Exclusive: Reflect Orbital Responds to its Critics
summary: Reflect Orbital faces criticism over its sunlight-reflecting satellites, sparking debate in the space community. The company has responded to these concerns.

title: NASA Opens Call on Moon Base Health Research
summary: NASA's Human Research Program is soliciting research proposals to address health challenges for long-term stays at a future Moon Base. This initiative aims to gather insights to support sustainable human presence on the lunar surface.

title: Rocket Lab Enters Europe’s Crowded Launch Market
summary: Rocket Lab is entering Europe's competitive launch market, surprising local companies as they return from holiday. The move marks Rocket Lab's expansion into a new region.

title: Exclusive: Space Kinetic Awarded $50M for Space Maneuverability
summary: Space Kinetic secured a $50 million OTA award from the U.S. Space Force to develop Whirlwind, a space maneuverability and deployment system. This funding highlights the growing investment in space technology and maneuverability capabilities.

title: Viasat Taps Rocket Lab to Build Small GEO for PTS-G Program
summary: Viasat has selected Rocket Lab to construct a small Geostationary Orbit (GEO) satellite for its Protected Tactical Satcom-Global (PTS-G) program. Rocket Lab will deliver the spacecraft based on its existing satellite platform.

title: Vietnam’s VinSpace Plans to Launch Tech Demonstration on 2027 SpaceX Rideshare Mission
summary: VinSpace, a Vietnamese space company under Vingroup, has signed a contract with SpaceX to launch in-orbit demonstration satellites on a 2027 Transporter rideshare mission. This marks a significant step for Vietnam's emerging space sector.

title: Aerospace Report Examines Defense and Space Growth in FY ‘27 Budget Request
summary: A new report from The Aerospace Corporation analyzes the White House's fiscal year 2027 budget request, highlighting that over 75% of the increase is allocated to defense and space sectors.

title: L3Harris Appoints Sam Mehta as New CEO After Kubasik Forced Out Due to Conduct
summary: L3Harris Technologies appointed Sam Mehta as its new president and CEO, replacing Chris Kubasik who was forced out due to conduct issues. The leadership change was effective immediately.

title: Seraphim Space Makes Hubble Investment
summary: Seraphim Space Investment Trust is investing $30 million into Hubble Network, which is developing a satellite-powered Bluetooth network using standard Bluetooth low energy chips.

title: Katalyst Space Wins U.S. Defense Innovation Unit Contract
summary: Katalyst Space has secured a contract from the U.S. Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) to develop deorbiting technologies. The agreement aims to leverage advanced space debris mitigation solutions for government applications.

title: Peru Taps Gilat for Connectivity Program
summary: Peru has awarded a $14 million connectivity deal to Gilat Satellite Networks. The agreement aims to enhance satellite connectivity in the country with a population of around 35 million people.

title: Lynk and Omnispace Completer Merger – Announce Elveo Mobile
summary: Lynk and Omnispace have completed their merger, forming a new combined company called Elveo Mobile. The merger aims to advance mobile satellite communications.

title: Sovereign Data at Tactical Speeds: BlackSky CTO Patrick O’Neil on the Shifts in Adoption of Space-based Intelligence
summary: Governments and military organizations are increasingly adopting space-based intelligence due to global conflicts, while BlackSky's CTO discusses the shifts in this adoption and the cost dynamics of satellite development.

title: Space Force Awards Space Data Network Contracts to Five Satellite Manufacturers
summary: The U.S. Space Force awarded contracts to five satellite manufacturers to develop a more diverse multi-vendor architecture for its space data network. This move aims to enhance the military's space capabilities through a broader supplier base.
